Opening

BUILD · Humanities · Autumn 1 · Week 4

Then and now photographs

Learning goal

Sort then and now photographs.

Who helps us belong to a community?

I can identify important people and places, describe a change, and explain one way I belong.

40 minutes, with flexible pauses. Point, speak, draw, type or write. A fictional example is welcome.

Editable Word pack
Arrival

BUILD · Humanities · Autumn 1 · Week 4

Arrival task

Choose a route for today. Begin with questions 1 and 2; continue when ready. Reading and scribing are available on every route.

Authored teaching pictures. Choose, point or explain.

1. Which phone has a dial that turns?

Help

Point to the dial or choose A. The diagrams are examples, not dated photographs.

A: the rotary telephone.

2. Does a black-and-white photo have to be older?

Help

Read or listen to the relevant evidence card; point first.

No. Use the source and date labels.

3. Find “present” in word help. What does it mean?

Help

Use the word and meaning cards together.

The time we are in now

4. How do you show a similarity?

Help

Use the source limit or map key as a clue.

Name a feature you can point to in both images.

1. Which phone has a dial that turns? Explain your choice.

Help

Point to the dial or choose A. The diagrams are examples, not dated photographs.

A: the rotary telephone.

2. Does a black-and-white photo have to be older?

Help

Use one source detail or labelled map feature.

No. Use the source and date labels.

3. Explain present using an example.

Help

Choose an example from the evidence cards.

The time we are in now Accept a relevant example.

4. How do you show a similarity?

Help

State the reason for your answer.

Name a feature you can point to in both images.

1. Which phone has a dial that turns? What can this teaching picture not tell us?

Help

Separate the illustration from historical or personal evidence.

A: the rotary telephone. It cannot establish a real person’s whole experience or belief.

2. Does a black-and-white photo have to be older? Give supporting evidence.

Help

Name the source or data label.

No. Use the source and date labels.

3. How does present help answer today’s enquiry?

Help

Explain the connection, not only the definition.

The time we are in now Accept a supported connection.

4. How do you show a similarity? Explain a limit or further check.

Help

Think about what the supplied evidence leaves uncertain.

Name a feature you can point to in both images.

Word and evidence bank

past
A time before now

present
The time we are in now

change
Something that becomes different

continuity
Something that stays the same

A · A fictional week

Monday: choose a club activity. Wednesday: practise the activity. Friday: share what was made. The words Monday, Wednesday and Friday supply the order.

Authored classroom case

Limit: This example does not describe every person or place.

B · Telephone comparison

A rotary telephone and a smartphone both support conversations over distance. A smartphone can also show a video call; a rotary dial selects numbers differently.

Authored comparison of familiar objects

Limit: A newer object is not automatically better for every person or purpose.

C · Photo enquiry

Use the paired local photographs supplied with this unit. Read the captions and dates. Point to one feature in each image before deciding what changed.

See photograph captions and credits

Limit: A camera angle or season can make features appear different; a photograph alone may not explain why.

D · Questions worth asking

Who used this object? When was this photo made? A dated catalogue entry can help with time; a user’s account can help with experience.

Authored classroom case

Limit: This example does not describe every person or place.

Starter

BUILD · Humanities · Autumn 1 · Week 4

Start the enquiry

Read the dates on the paired bridge photographs.

Tees Transporter Bridge. The viewpoints differ. Compare gondola position and the blue steel structure; do not infer permanent rebuilding from camera angle. Neither photograph is a live view of today.

Choose help or a further challenge

Choose one feature in each example and use the same feature to compare.

Complete both sides before writing a similarity and a difference.

Consider viewpoint, source selection and variation within groups.

    Independent

    BUILD · Humanities · Autumn 1 · Week 4

    Independent application

    Choose one route. Complete the required outcome with the support you need.

    Supported task

    1. Sort the two dated photographs into then and later.
    2. Caption one visible change and one similarity.
    3. Use the image labels as evidence.
    Begin with one step. Read the sources with an adult, reduce the visible choice set and use: Photo ___ is earlier. The ___ changed. Both show ___.

    Keep all required evidence; speech, pointing, drawing and exact scribing are available.

    Standard task

    1. Sort the two dated photographs into then and later.
    2. Caption one visible change and one similarity.
    3. Use the image labels as evidence.
    Photo ___ is earlier. The ___ changed. Both show ___.

    Check your evidence before adding a final explanation.

    Stretch task

    1. Sort the two dated photographs into then and later.
    2. Caption one visible change and one similarity.
    3. Use the image labels as evidence.
    Plan your answer using the source labels. Use the frame if useful.

    Explain how angle or image quality might limit one comparison.

    Then and now photographs

    BUILD · Autumn 1 · Week 4

    Goal: Sort then and now photographs.

    Enquiry

    Who helps us belong to a community?

    past
    A time before now

    present
    The time we are in now

    change
    Something that becomes different

    continuity
    Something that stays the same

    Key knowledge

    1. No. Use the source and date labels.
    2. Name a feature you can point to in both images.

    Method

    Photo ___ is earlier. The ___ changed. Both show ___.

    Remember

    Use date and source labels to establish order. Image colour is not proof of age. A fictional personal timeline is always allowed.
